intro.title: usePrevious
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `usePrevious` that tracks the previous value of a state or prop. You'll learn the core concept of storing a value from a previous render cycle using the `useRef` and `useEffect` hooks. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the React Hooks API. By the end, you'll understand how to capture and compare previous values, a common pattern for handling changes in functional components. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to creating reusable custom hooks with TypeScript.
intro.usecase: The usePrevious hook is essential for tracking state changes in real-world React applications. In dashboards, it helps detect when metric values cross thresholds to trigger alerts or visual highlights. In forms, it enables comparing current and previous field values to show validation feedback only when data actually changes. This pattern is also valuable in interactive UI components like sliders or toggles, where developers need to respond to specific state transitions rather than just current values.
